bib.title: Toward Autonomous Long-Horizon Engineering for ML Research

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Toward Autonomous Long-Horizon Engineering for ML Research" (system: AiScientist), Guoxin Chen, Jie Chen, Lei Chen, Jiale Zhao, Fanzhe Meng, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ruihua Song, Cheng Chen, Ji-Rong Wen, Kai Jia (Renmin Univ. / AweAI). arXiv:2604.13018v2 [cs.CL], preprint, dated Apr. 15 2026 (v2 26 May 2026).

COVERAGE: All 20 of 20 pages, 59,975 of 59,975 chars, read via pypdf. This includes the references and Appendices A-E (related work, File-as-Bus schema Table 3, metric definitions, baseline details, supplementary figs). The Figure 1 and Figure 3 axis text is garbled in the extraction. There is no limitations section, and the paper does not describe any failure analysis.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: A File-as-Bus workspace (durable schema-governed artifacts) is the key driver. Removing it hurts MLE-Bench Lite far more than PaperBench, and the damage falls on later-round refinement.
  number: -31.82 Any Medal points on MLE-Bench Lite, -6.41 PaperBench points
  setup: GLM-5 backbone, 24 h, one H20 GPU per task; ablation in Fig 4. The paper gives no ablation table, only a figure.
  quote: "Removing File-as-Bus causes large degradation on both benchmarks. On PaperBench, average score drops by 6.41 points. On MLE-Bench Lite, Any Medal drops by 31.82 points."
  where: p9, Sec 4.5
- claim: Valid Submission and Bronze stay largely intact without File-as-Bus. Durable state matters for diagnosing and improving over later rounds, not for producing a first runnable result.
  number: none
  setup: MLE-Bench Lite, GLM-5
  quote: "Valid Submission and Bronze remain largely intact, while Above Median, Silver, Gold, and Any Medal degrade much more."
  where: p9
- claim: AiScientist beats the matched baselines on the full 20-task PaperBench, and costs less per task than IterativeAgent.
  number: 30.52 vs 20.60 (Gemini-3-Flash, +9.92); 33.73 vs 22.37 (GLM-5, +11.15)
  setup: Gemini-3-Flash and GLM-5 backbones; one H20, 24 h per task; grader GPT-5.4; single run, no error bars.
  quote: "Average Score 29.45 19.26 20.60 30.52+9.92 22.58 22.3733.73+11.15"
  where: p7, Table 1
- claim: Cost per task. AiScientist is cheaper than IterativeAgent, and more rounds alone do not explain the gain.
  number: $15.67 vs $27.44 (Gemini); $12.20 vs $54.90 (GLM-5)
  setup: PaperBench, same as above. A full 20-task eval costs about $832 to grade.
  quote: "$15.67 versus $27.44 per task under Gemini-3-Flash, and $12.20 versus $54.90 under GLM-5."
  where: p7, Sec 4.2
- claim: AiScientist reaches the same Any Medal% under both backbones on MLE-Bench Lite. It beats the strongest matched baseline and the Codex reference.
  number: 81.82 Any Medal%, +4.55 (Gemini) and +16.67 (GLM-5); +13.64 over Codex
  setup: 22 tasks, 24 h, one H20; mean ± SEM over 3 seeds. Matched baselines are AIDE, LoongFlow, ML-Master 2.0. Codex is GPT-5.5 xhigh, a reference and not matched.
  quote: "AiScientist reaches 81.82 Any Medal% under both backbones, improving over the strongest matched baseline by 4.55 points with Gemini-3-Flash and 16.67 points with GLM-5."
  where: p7, Sec 4.3
- claim: Codex/GPT-5.5 xhigh is a strong reference. On PaperBench it scores 29.45 against the best AiScientist's 33.73 (+4.28). On MLE-Bench Lite it scores 68.18 Any Medal.

  setup: reference harness, not matched

  number: +4.74 PaperBench; +22.73 Above Median and +9.09 Any Medal on MLE-Bench Lite
  setup: GLM-5, Fig 4
  quote: "AiScientist without File-as-Bus still improves average score by 4.74 points over the simpler agent baseline, while on MLE-Bench Lite it improves Above Median by 22.73 points and Any Medal by 9.09 points."
  where: p9

  number: 27% of runs converged by 6 h, 44% by 12 h (Fig 3c)
  setup: MLE-Bench Lite, GLM-5. The percentages are read off the figure text.

  where: p1, Fig 1

DESIGN (for the note)
- "Thin control over thick state". The Orchestrator (Tier 0) holds only concise summaries, directives and a compact workspace map. Detail lives in files.
- Two continuity requirements. Role continuity: a re-invoked specialist resumes from its own prior artifacts. Project continuity: roles coordinate around shared evidence, not lossy conversational handoffs.
- Agent-as-Tool. Specialists sit in the Orchestrator's action space (a_t in T0 ∪ A1). Each returns a concise summary plus workspace updates.
- Tiers. Tier-1 specialists are Paper Comprehension, Prioritization, Implementation and Experimentation, plus a Generic Helper. Tier-2 subagents handle bounded subtasks. The hierarchy is not recursive.
- Three artifact update modes. Append-only logs (impl_log.md, exp_log.md), versioned artifacts (plans, paper_analysis/*), and mutable state (code, setup scripts, reproduce.sh).
- Schema (Table 3). Each artifact declares its purpose, update mode, writers and readers. Access is role-scoped, and Tier-2 subagents are read-only by default.
- Workspace map. It is refreshed after each specialist invocation and works as an index, so agents read other artifacts on demand.
- The loop. Build a scaffold, then alternate implement and experiment. The Orchestrator picks the next fix from the recorded evidence.

LIMITS
- No limitations section. The authors concede that PaperBench full evaluation is costly (~$832) and "materially limits large-scale repeated evaluation".
- PaperBench rows are single full runs with no seeds or error bars. MLE-Bench Lite uses 3 seeds.
- Only two backbones, both cheaper or open models (Gemini-3-Flash, GLM-5). Codex/GPT-5.5 is a reference, not matched, and it differs in model and harness.
- The File-as-Bus ablation is shown in a figure only. It has no numbers in a table and no separate figure of the "simpler agent".
- Gains over Codex are mixed. Codex uses far fewer steps and is competitive early. Leaderboard rows come from other protocols.
- The "no File-as-Bus" ablation changes the whole coordination mechanism. It does not separate the individual artifact types, and the schema design choices are not ablated.
- Domain is ML research engineering, with 24 h tasks and one H20 GPU. Generalisation to other long-horizon work is unshown.
- The authors describe the evidence as "suggests", and the causal claims are interpretive (Sec 4.6).

BUILDS ON: PaperBench (Starace et al., 2025); MLE-Bench (Chan et al., 2025); AIDE (Jiang et al., 2025); ML-Master 2.0 (Zhu et al., 2026); LoongFlow (Wan et al., 2025); The AI Scientist (Lu et al., 2024) and v2 (Yamada et al., 2025); Agent Laboratory (Schmidgall et al., 2025); CAMEL (Li et al., 2023), MetaGPT (Hong et al., 2023), ChatDev (Qian et al., 2024); multi-agent failure analyses (Cemri et al., 2025; Yan et al., 2025; Tang et al., 2026).

CODE: none. The code is only in the supplementary material, per App C. The paper's Fig 2 shows this workspace layout: `~/paper_analysis` (summary.md, algorithm.md, structure.md, baseline.md, experiments.md), `~/submission` (the repo, setup scripts, reproduce.sh), `~/agent` (prioritized_task.md, impl_log.md [append only], exp_log.md [append only], experiments/).

FIGURES
- Fig 2 (p4). Architecture: Orchestrator, specialists, subagents, File-as-Bus workspace and its permission tiers. It is the fastest summary of thin control over thick state.
- Fig 3 (p9). Anytime score, pairwise lead rate and time-to-final-best on MLE-Bench Lite, GLM-5. It shows the late-refinement effect.
- Fig 4 (p9). Ablation bars for the simpler agent, AiScientist, and AiScientist without File-as-Bus. It shows that validity survives but medals do not.
- Figs 5, 6 (p10-11). Workflow-step allocation per stage.
- Table 3 (p17). The File-as-Bus artifact schema.
- Figs 7 and 8 (p20) are supplementary delegation and budget views.

PROBLEMS: Garbled axis text for Fig 1, Fig 3 and Fig 8 in the extraction, so the percentages for 6 h and 12 h come from caption-adjacent text. In Table 1 some cells (e.g. the "bold" markers) run into neighbouring numbers, and the bold best-cell is unmarked. No embedded instructions were found. The Table 1 columns are Codex, then Gemini (Basic, Iter, AiScientist), then GLM (Basic, Iter, AiScientist); the merged row text is ambiguous for a few tasks, so rely only on the Average row.
